service.description: A deployable service or component within a bounded context.

id.description: Stable service id (SVC###) - makes the service a first-class, referenceable graph node.

kind.description: Architectural component type. Determines applicable contract patterns.

system_ref.description: The system party (PRT###) this service is a component of. A service nested under a party is a component of that party and may omit it; naming a different party there is a cross-reference error. A service under a root-declared context names it here or inherits the document's `system_ref` default, and one that does neither is reported by the semantic checker as a service without a system. Distinct from `owned_by`, which says who owns the service rather than what it is part of.

imports.description: The libraries this service is built on: a package it imports or a component it embeds, so that its build contains them. Each item names, by its exact declared id, scope prefix included, either another service, normally one of `kind: library`, for a library the organization builds, or a third-party package (PKG###) declared in a `packages:` list; an item that names nothing declared is a cross-reference error. One list holds both, and the model graph draws a `service_imports` edge to each named service or package, so impact analysis reaches every service built on a changed library. A call over an interface to a running service is not an import: state it in `uses`, and in the contracts once they are written. Optional.

uses.description: The services this one depends on while running, stated at the level of a container diagram ("orders uses payments"): the statement to make before the contracts between the two are written. Each item names another service by its exact declared id, scope prefix included; an item that names no declared service is a cross-reference error. The model graph draws a `service_uses` edge to each named service, so impact analysis reaches every service that depends on a changed one. A library this service is built on belongs in `imports`. Once contracts are written, they state the operations, direction and transport of the dependency. Optional.

summary.description: Brief description of what this service does.

description.description: Full description of this service's purpose, responsibilities, and domain role.

vendor.description: Teams or vendors responsible for this service.

resource_refs.description: Typed infrastructure resources this service requires (IR### - `infra_resource_ref`), resolving to `resource` entities in the infrastructure layer. This is the canonical *intent* edge to a CONCRETE resource; the infrastructure layer's `hosted_on` relation is the *placement* edge. Optional. Since v2.8 it is the only way a service names its resources: the free-string `resources` list is no longer accepted. See `needs` for the abstract (type-level) intent.

needs.description: Abstract infrastructure NEEDS (Score `type`/`class`/`id`/`params` vocabulary) this service declares - TYPE-level intent, resolved to a concrete resource per environment by a binding (BND###). The three altitudes: `needs` (type) → binding (type × environment) → `resource_refs` / `resource` (IR### instance). A need names WHAT the service requires without pinning a platform, so the same need realizes on cloud, on-prem, or hybrid. Additive/optional (v2.7.7).

servers.description: Server instances where this service is deployed. Follows OpenAPI server object pattern.

environment.description: Which deployment environment this server instance serves. A value takes exactly one of three forms, and the three cannot overlap: a name from the common vocabulary (production, staging, development, test); a typed environment reference (ENV###) naming an environment the model declares, so the server points at the entity carrying that environment's class, substrate, provider and target scope; or an `x-` prefixed name, for an environment outside the common vocabulary. Only the typed form resolves - naming an ENV### the model does not declare is a cross-reference error, while a name is checked against nothing.

protocol.description: Protocol if different from service default.

contracts.description: External contracts exposing and consuming interfaces for this service.

side_effects.description: Observable side effects beyond request/response: filesystem, stdout, stderr.

implementation.description: Whether this service exists yet. Absent means unclear.

provenance.description: Epistemic provenance for this service (brownfield modeling confidence).

infra_relation_edge.description: A typed inter-resource relation (TOSCA vocabulary). `hosted_on` is the canonical placement edge; `connects_to`/`depends_on` may carry attribute-level output refs; `depends_on` is the ordering-only fallback. A `network-link` resource's connects_to/routes_to targets may sit in a different environment/substrate (the hybrid boundary).

type.description: TOSCA relation verb: hosted_on / connects_to / depends_on / attaches_to / routes_to.

target.description: The target resource (IR###). May be in another environment/substrate (hybrid interconnect).

outputs.description: Optional attribute-level outputs of the target this resource consumes - e.g. host, port, connection-string. Makes connects_to/depends_on wiring explicit for impact analysis.

description.description: Optional human note on this edge (e.g. 'reads via read-replica').
